content.user_title: Build Functional React Apps with fp-ts
content.value_statement: React apps often mix nulls, failed requests, and async states in fragile ways. This skill gives practical fp-ts patterns for safer state, validation, data fetching, and rendering.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use Option, Either, TaskEither, RemoteData, and pipe in React code.
Shows React hook patterns for missing values, async requests, and loading states.
Demonstrates form validation with Either and accumulated field errors.
Covers referential stability when fp-ts values interact with React rendering.
Includes dependency injection, testing, and React 19 examples for functional components.
limitations: It is a documentation skill, not a runtime package or code generator.
Examples require adaptation to the user project and dependency versions.
It does not verify API contracts, accessibility, or production security controls.
It assumes basic React, TypeScript, and fp-ts familiarity for advanced sections.

use_cases.title: Add fp-ts to a React Feature
use_cases.description: Use Option and Either to replace nullable state and scattered validation checks.

use_cases.title: Standardize Async UI States
use_cases.description: Model loading, failure, and success paths with TaskEither and RemoteData patterns.

use_cases.title: Review Functional React Patterns
use_cases.description: Compare component examples against safer fp-ts patterns before merging changes.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: I am building a React component with a value that might be missing. Show how to use fp-ts Option cleanly.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor my React form validation to use fp-ts Either and return all field errors at once.

prompt_templates.title: Model Data Fetching
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a React hook that uses TaskEither and RemoteData for loading, error, retry, and success states.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Feature Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React feature for fp-ts usage, referential stability, dependency injection, and React 19 compatibility.

output_examples.input: A signup form needs email, password, and name validation with clear field errors.
output_examples.output: The response explains an Either-based validation flow, lists each validation rule, and describes how the component displays accumulated errors.

output_examples.input: A profile page needs loading, retry, error, and success rendering for a user request.
output_examples.output: The response outlines a RemoteData state model and shows how each state maps to a distinct React view.

output_examples.input: A component re-renders too often after introducing Option values.
output_examples.output: The response identifies referential instability and recommends memoization or stable fp-ts-aware hooks.

best_practices: Use Option for missing values instead of mixing null and undefined in component state.
Use RemoteData when a view has loading, failure, and success states.
Memoize fp-ts values when React dependency arrays depend on stable references.
anti_patterns: Do not use fp-ts types only for style when simpler TypeScript is clearer.
Do not model async UI with unrelated loading, error, and data booleans.
Do not skip tests after refactoring validation or data fetching logic.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps apply fp-ts patterns to React state, forms, data fetching, rendering, and testing.

faq.question: Does it install any packages?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Users choose whether to install referenced libraries.

faq.question: Can it work with Next.js?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance targets React and includes patterns suitable for modern Next.js applications.

faq.question: Is it only for expert fp-ts users?
faq.answer: No. It starts with basic Option and Either usage, then moves into advanced patterns.

faq.question: Can it replace project-specific tests?
faq.answer: No. The examples still need local tests, type checks, and production review.
